name: Pavel Nedvěd (Pavel Nedved)
years: Born 30 Aug 1972. Ballon d'Or 2003. Playing career 1990-2009 (Plzen, Dukla Prague, Sparta Prague, Kosice, Lazio, Juventus). Czech national team 1994-2006, 91 caps, 18 goals. Since 2025: general manager of the Czech national teams (FAČR).

limits: Spain-away date (3 Oct) was confirmed by the Bolavip preview in the fact check. The Czech-home-Croatia date is not stated in any checked source and is not used.
No direct YouTube search was possible. viral_moments carry article links; YouTube links are given only where one was actually found, otherwise a search phrase is supplied.
Several Czech news pages returned 403 (infotbal.cz, fotbal.cz, tn.nova.cz). Facts from them are only used where another readable source confirms them.

recent_news.headline: FIFA ranking: Czechia falls to 53rd, lowest since 2017
facts: The November 2026 FIFA ranking (published 18 Nov) puts Czechia 53rd with 1,451 points.
A year and a quarter earlier (Sept 2025) the team was 39th, so it lost 14 places; it is the lowest spot since Sept 2017 (58th).
Czechia now ranks behind Slovakia (47th), Slovenia (49th) and Peru (52nd); Austria is 22nd, Hungary 37th, Poland 38th.

recent_news.headline: Poborský: Czechia cannot play Spanish football, worst losing run in national history
facts: Karel Poborsky said he sees only a continued search for a line-up, that it should have looked different long ago, and that the coach will have to give some ground (compromise).
The seven-match losing run (Mexico at the World Cup plus six Nations League games) is the longest in Czech and Czechoslovak national team history.
Across the two November games Czechia had one shot on target; in Osijek Croatia had 8 shots on target to Czechia's 1.

recent_news.headline: Nedvěd: Denia has full confidence, firing is not up for discussion
facts: After the sixth straight defeat Nedvěd told ČT Sport that a coaching change is not on the agenda and the team is being rebuilt.

He said the federation has full confidence in Denia and admitted quality is missing; the 37 players used this autumn, 12 of them complete debutants, is a figure Nedvěd gave that was reported in the 17 Nov SportyZive/Tiscali piece (not in this article).
Nedvěd cannot sack the coach alone but can propose it; the FAČR executive committee decides. One commentary calls Denia largely Nedvěd's choice.

recent_news.headline: Croatia 2-1 Czechia in Osijek: six defeats from six, relegated from Nations League A
facts: Czechia finished the Nations League A3 group with 0 points, 3 goals scored and 14 conceded (goal difference -11).
England and Spain finished on 15 points each, Croatia on 6 (relegation play-off).
Three red cards in six games: Šulc (25', v England), and Krejčí twice (once at Spain, once at home v Spain).

recent_news.headline: Czechia 0-2 Spain in Prague, Krejčí sent off after VAR review
facts: Match played at Letná, Prague, on Thursday 12 November; Czechia entered it with four straight defeats and no points.
Krejčí's yellow was upgraded to a red card by VAR in the 72nd minute.
Spain had already qualified for the quarter-finals.

recent_news.headline: Nedvěd calls out Sparta: no Sparta player in the Czech squad for the first time since 2022
facts: Nedvěd said it was a problem that no Sparta player was in the November squad; it is the first time since November 2022.
He said Sparta sometimes starts with only one or two Czech players and that he spoke to the club leadership.
He also said the door is open for Patrik Schick, but the team did not contact him before this camp.

recent_news.headline: Slovak tabloids relayed: Nedvěd's adult children missed the September wedding
facts: A Time News rewrite of Slovak entertainment reports says his two adult children were absent from the wedding, reportedly staying in Florida.
Dara Rolins reportedly said it is a private matter and everyone is on good terms.
The article offers speculation only and no confirmed evidence of any family conflict.

recent_news.headline: England 3-0 Czechia at Wembley: Kane brace, Coufal own goal
facts: Vladimír Coufal put a Harry Kane cross into his own net on 27 minutes; Kane then scored in the 40th and 57th minutes.
England had 65% possession and 17 shots to Czechia's 5.
Kane's two goals took his England tally to 91 goals in 125 caps.

recent_news.headline: Spain 3-1 Czechia in Oviedo: Krejčí sent off for a second yellow
facts: Spain beat Czechia 3-1 on 3 October (date confirmed by the Bolavip preview) in the first of the two meetings.
Krejčí was sent off for a second yellow card (85th minute per the Tiscali results table; another report only says he was sent off, so the minute is not fully certain).
Per Fotbalportal, Czechia had no shot on target at Wembley (England) or in the home game v Spain; seven shots on target in six games overall.

recent_news.headline: Czechia 0-2 England in Prague: Šulc sent off after 25 minutes
facts: Anthony Gordon (47') and Harry Kane (69') scored; it was England's first Nations League win (second attempt).
Pavel Šulc's yellow card was upgraded to a red by VAR for a high lunge on Elliot Anderson in the 25th minute.
Sky Sports report dated 30 September; the match itself was most likely played on the evening of 29 September (not stated directly).

recent_news.headline: Nedvěd to Schick's criticism: 'I'm not one who looks for alibis'
facts: Schick had criticised the World Cup logistics (insufficient recovery, heavy travel).
Nedvěd said the travel was set by FIFA and may have affected the team, but that results are decided on the pitch.
He said the federation added a nutrition adviser for the Nations League camp, and that Schick has no interest in playing for the national team.

recent_news.headline: Denia names first squad: 11 new or returning players, Schick absent
facts: Santi Denia, first foreign coach of the Czech A-team, announced his first Nations League squad on 18 September.
Of the 26 World Cup players, 15 kept their place; Staněk, Souček, Darida, Chytil and Schick, among others, were left out.
Nedvěd said final sporting decisions belong to Denia and he acts as a support partner with context and data.

recent_news.headline: Nedvěd marries singer Dara Rolins (reportedly in Italy)
facts: The couple married on Wednesday 2 September 2026; Blesk says clues point to Italy (Lake Maggiore area) but the location was not explicitly confirmed.
Rolins confirmed it on Instagram with a photo of the rings and kept her own surname.
The relationship was first confirmed in December 2021; he proposed at the end of 2024 in Livigno.

recent_news.headline: Schick says the national team's World Cup logistics wore players down
facts: Patrik Schick sharply criticised travel and recovery at the World Cup; the piece is cited as a 28 August report.
Nedvěd answered three weeks later (see 18 Sept item).

Tiscali reports Schick ended his national team career after the tournament; Nedvěd said in September that Schick has no interest in playing for the team. The earlier '26 goals in 56 caps' figure could not be verified and was removed.
recent_news.note: Date confirmed: the 18 Sept iSport article links the original Schick piece ('Schick ostře: Nároďák nás znehodnocoval') dated 28 Aug 2026.

recent_news.headline: Chovanec reportedly claims Nedvěd ended Koubek's reign with 'one phone call'
facts: An article on 25 Aug 2026 cites a podcast from 27 Jan 2026 in which Jozef Chovanec describes Nedvěd's informal influence in Czech football.
The exact 'single call' wording could not be found in a public transcript; treat as allegation, not fact.
FAČR chairman Trunda said on 2 July that Nedvěd's departure was not on the table.
recent_news.note: Unverified allegation. Do not state as fact in the script.

recent_news.headline: FAČR appoints Santi Denia, the first foreign national team coach
facts: Spaniard Santi Denia (Olympic gold with Spain in 2024) signed a two-year contract with an option to extend.
Nedvěd said he hoped Denia would help give the team a new identity.
Older than 90 days, kept because it explains the current Nations League story.

recent_news.headline: Nedvěd admits mistakes after World Cup group-stage exit
facts: In an iSport interview Nedvěd said the team went out deservedly and that he saw tired players but did not push hard enough to change things.
He said he was annoyed that Rosický criticised Schick during the tournament.
Older than 90 days; context for the later Denia and Schick stories.

recent_news.headline: Italian court accepts Nedvěd's plea deal in Juventus accounts case
facts: A Rome judge accepted plea deals; Nedvěd received a suspended sentence of 1 year 2 months, Agnelli 1 year 8 months, Juventus a 156,000 euro fine.
Under Italian law a plea deal is not an admission of guilt, and the defendants denied wrongdoing.
FAČR said the ruling does not affect his job. Old and legal: background only, never a joke.

now.role: General manager of the Czech national teams (A team and U21) at the Czech FA (FAČR), appointed June 2025. Not a coach: he proposes coaches and manages the set-up, while the FAČR executive committee decides on firing.
now.club_or_contract: No club job found. Wikipedia lists a Jan 2025 Al Shabab sporting-director role (stale next to the national team role). Forbes reports he is leaving the Fotbal HK 1905 (Hradec Králové) ownership group; its date, the reason and the share split were not verifiable. Contract length not found.
this_season_in_numbers: World Cup 2026 (first for Czechia in 20 years, reached via March playoff wins on penalties over Ireland and Denmark): 1 point from 3 games, out in the group stage, 0-3 loss to Mexico.
Nations League A3 autumn 2026 under new coach Denia: 6 matches, 0 points, 3 goals for, 14 against, relegated to League B.
Seven straight defeats counting Mexico, the longest losing run in Czech and Czechoslovak history.
Three red cards in six Nations League games (Šulc once, Krejčí twice).
FIFA ranking 53rd (39th in Sept 2025), lowest since 2017.
37 players used this autumn, 12 of them debutants.
now.what_people_say: Critics (Vízek, Hynek, Chovanec's reported remarks) question his management and some say he should go; Poborský says the team is still only searching for a line-up and the coach will have to give some ground. Nedvěd and FAČR say Denia has full confidence and there is no talk of change. Next: Euro 2028 qualifying draw on 6 December 2026, with Czechia outside the top pot.

quick_context: Nedvěd won Serie A with Lazio in 2000 and with Juventus in 2002 and 2003, after starting at Sparta Prague.
In 2002-03 he made 43 appearances and scored 14 goals in all competitions, and won the 2003 Ballon d'Or even though he missed the Champions League final through suspension.
He earned 91 caps and 18 goals for Czechia and captained the team to the Euro 2004 semi-final.
roast_past: The hair: the long blond mane and the 'Furia Ceca' / 'Méďa' (Little Bear) nicknames from Italian and Czech fans.
Sent off three times in his first six matches at Sparta, while critics later called him overly aggressive and accused of diving.
Won the Ballon d'Or in the same season he watched the Champions League final from the stands, suspended after a semi-final booking.
Euro 1996 final lost to Germany on a golden goal; Euro 2004 semi-final lost to Greece. A big golden career without a major national team trophy.
Came out of international retirement for the 2006 World Cup and Czechia still finished third in their group.
Famous long-hair perfectionist who later ran the Prague Half Marathon (2010) and Prague Marathon (2012): never stopped running, just changed the shirt.

Left Juventus as a player, came back as vice chairman, left again with the board in 2022 - a career in the same building, with different coats (jokes about career moves only, never about the legal case).
roast_now: He hired the first foreign coach in Czech history, and the new coach opened with six defeats from six: zero points, 3 goals scored, 14 conceded.
Seven defeats in a row is now the longest losing run in Czech and Czechoslovak national team history, and it started under his previous coach.
A national team that once had a Ballon d'Or winner now has one shot on target in two November games.
Three red cards in six matches: the old tackler would approve of the style, the scoreboard would not.
He said he does not look for alibis, in the same breath as adding a nutrition adviser to the camp.
He criticised Sparta for starting with only one or two Czech players, while the national team used 37 players this autumn, 12 of them debutants.
The FIFA ranking fell from 39th to 53rd, behind Slovakia, Slovenia and Peru.
'Full confidence' in the coach, 'not up for discussion': the loyal friend of a man with 0 points.
praise: Ballon d'Or 2003, the second Czech winner after Josef Masopust and the first since Czechoslovakia split.
2002-03: 43 appearances and 14 goals in all competitions, Serie A title, Serie A Footballer of the Year (shared with Totti), World Soccer Player of the Year.
91 caps and 18 goals for Czechia, captain at Euro 2004 and named in the Team of the Tournament.
In the 2006-07 Serie B season, with Juventus in the second tier, he stayed and scored 11 league goals as the club won the title.
Career total: 501 league appearances and 110 goals; Czech Footballer of the Year four times, UEFA Team of the Year in 2003, 2004 and 2005.
As general manager, the Czech team reached the 2026 World Cup, its first in 20 years, after playoff wins on penalties over Ireland and Denmark.
no_joke_topics: Juventus false-accounting case, the plea deal, the suspended sentence, the Italian football ban and any 'legal troubles' wording (news only if needed, never a joke).
Calciopoli and the revoked Juventus titles (club legal history).
Family: marriage to Dara Rolins, the wedding, the divorce from his first wife, his children (Ivana, Pavel Jr.), Ivana's engagement, and any rumour of family friction.
Health, injuries and exhaustion of players (the World Cup 'tired players' story is a sporting story, but no jokes about anyone's body or health).
Doping, war, politics, and Schick's personal reasons for leaving the national team.
Unverified allegations such as the Chovanec 'one phone call' claim: do not repeat as fact.

flipbook_ideas: Seven red-and-white shirts fall one after another like dominoes, ending on a tiny 'FIFA 53' sign (tied to the seven straight defeats and ranking drop).
A caricature Nedvěd with the long blond mane sweeps the pitch like a broom, collecting a pile of three red cards (tied to the three sendings off; no health or family angle).
Cartoon scoreboard showing 3-14 where the '3' is drawn as a tiny sad number next to a big '14' balloon.
Caricature Nedvěd holds a 'FULL CONFIDENCE' umbrella over a coach while rain falls as zeroes (0 points).
One lone shot on target drawn as a small sad football dribbling toward a huge Croatian goalkeeper (tied to the single shot on target in November).
Nedvěd in the 2003 Ballon d'Or pose swapping places with a bored GM in a suit, same blond mane both ways (past vs present).

image_reference_notes.signature_look: Long blond hair worn loose or pushed back, lean athletic build, intense serious face, strong jaw; Italian fans called him 'Furia Ceca'.
image_reference_notes.current_look: UNVERIFIED: no reliable photo description of his 2026 look was found in the sources used. Public photos usually show short, grey-tinged hair and business wear as general manager; confirm with a current press photo before drawing.
image_reference_notes.kit_colours: Juventus black-and-white stripes (No. 11), Lazio sky blue, Sparta dark red, Czech Republic red with white and blue accents.
image_reference_notes.expressions: Fierce, tight-lipped determination; pointing and shouting at teammates; rare broad smile.
image_reference_notes.signature_pose: Running full tilt with fist clenched and long hair flying; also arms pumping after a goal; as GM, hands folded and serious expression at press tables.

verification.notes: Adversarial check on 2026-11-20 by opening cited URLs (Tiscali, iSport, Blesk, ČTK/ceskenoviny, Sky, Sports Mole, Bolavip, Irish Examiner, Echo24, Praguedaily, Wikipedia en/cs). Confirmed: FIFA rank 53rd/1,451 and 39th in Sept 2025; A3 table (ENG 15, ESP 15, CRO 6, CZE 0; GF 3, GA 14); all six scores; 3 red cards; seven-loss run; 37 players/12 debutants; Denia appointed 31 Jul, two-year deal; WC playoffs v Ireland/Denmark on penalties and 0-3 v Mexico with 1 point; Euro 2028 draw 6 Dec in Belfast; plea deal terms; Ballon d'Or and career stats. Corrected: wedding location only reported, not confirmed; Hradec Králové entry removed (no date, shares or reason in Forbes); Schick '26 goals in 56 caps' removed; Poborský 'did not call for sacking' unsupported; shots-on-target wording for Oct games; Sept match date likely 29 Sept; Koubek claim re Nedvěd staying; career start 1990; Serie A Footballer of the Year was shared with Totti; Rosický dispute is one-sided. Remaining gaps: Spain-away Krejčí red minute (85' in one table, other source unclear); Al Shabab exit not documented; GM start date June 2025 only from cs.wikipedia (tribuna 403); WebSearch budget exhausted, so independent-search checks were limited to opened URLs; the checker could not open fotbal.cz/infotbal.cz.
